Favorite stretches pre and post a good ride?

Does opening a beer count as a post ride stretch?

But, really I usually don't stretch before or after..

To stretch, I ride my bike. It really loosens me up for more bike riding.

Sometimes after a lot of riding, when I get off the bike, I'll swing my arms and rock my torso back and forth. I think it helps the arms and lower back. I'm not sure.

If you have knee problems, I hear leg stretches in general are good to do before getting on the bike. In particular, there's one stretch where you bend one knee while leaning yourself forward onto a post or a tree or something. I hear that does wonders.

It's also good to strengthen your muscles. Having good core strength and strong leg muscles are important, but your overall strength does play a part in preventing you from feeling strained and sore. I had some issues when I first started riding, but I also started working in body weight exercises like squats, dips, pushups, pullups, etc. After building up some strength that way, my issues pretty much went away.

Also, making sure to have a good bike fit, having the correct position on the bike, paying particular attention to the position and angle of your feet, shifting hand positions on the bars, and getting out of the saddle occasionally, are all things you can do to make your ride more comfortable.

In short, I don't really do stretches. They definitely can have benefits, but there are other things to mind which may have a far greater impact.

After a ride... no. After a shower and before I sleep... yes.

I make sure to work my least flexible area which is the area behind the knee. I raise one of my leg onto a countertop that's close to 90degrees, make sure to square my hip, contract my shin so my feet point towards me, then reach and hold.

Then I do a variation where I rotate my hip out and reach down and below the countertop. This stretches my inner thigh.

One I just love doing is where I sit down, cross my leg over the other and using the crossed leg as leverage torque my back and crack crack crack crack crack. Repeat for other side.

I do a multitude of stretches but those two + 1 are my favorites.
